bull.b: A 15-year triple-net lease for 352 MW IT with a $9.8B base-term (3% escalator and renewal options) converts greenfield delivery into long-duration, investment-grade cash flows. This materially de-risks revenue timing and supports repeatable project economics and lender confidence over years.

The $3.25B River Bend financing (16.5-yr, high LTV, investment-grade ratings, non-callable) validates a non‑recourse, capital‑efficient funding model. Long-dated, project-level debt reduces parent refinancing exposure and enables equity recycling, increasing long-term funding predictability.

bull.t: Large, repeatable development pipeline & power‑first model
bull.b: An 8.4 GW pipeline and demonstrated commercialization of two AI campuses indicate scalable, repeatable execution under a power‑first model. If delivered, the pipeline supports sustained contracted NOI growth and long-term capacity monetization beyond volatile BTC mining cycles.

bear.t: Rapid rise in debt and leverage
bear.b: Debt jumped dramatically to ~$7.7B, materially increasing leverage relative to equity. High absolute indebtedness raises refinancing and covenant risk, limits strategic flexibility, and amplifies the impact of interest rate moves and cash‑flow shortfalls over the medium term.

bear.t: Weak cash generation and negative free cash flow
bear.b: Sustained negative operating cash flow and deeply negative free cash flow imply the business cannot self‑fund growth or cover obligations without external capital. Persistent cash burn increases reliance on project financing and capital markets, raising execution and dilution risks over time.

bear.t: Earnings volatility & delayed infrastructure revenue ramp
bear.b: Unrealized mark‑to‑market swings from digital assets create headline earnings volatility that obscures operating trends and weakens credit metrics. At the same time, material infrastructure revenue and NOI won't arrive until project delivery (~Q2 2027), leaving a multi‑quarter exposure window.
